comparison_limits: Eight named GPU points are not whole-material measurements.
GPU reports are the latest asynchronous sample every 30 frames; the screenshot frame is not explicitly recorded, so exact sample/frame correspondence is unproven.
Automatic adaptation channels are spatially sampled history. A constant override removes that spatial variation as well as temporal response.
CPU counterfactuals change only the bloom vector at the measured source and actual A; they do not predict all regional pixels or validate retail producers.
Changing specular can change scene inputs, bloom and automatic adaptation. Source and A deltas remain explicit.
Final endpoint counts do not locate clipping without corresponding GPU evidence; a single clamped point does not locate every regional hotspot.
The historical complaint comparison changes engine and adds diagnostics. It is a bounded repeat, not an isolated bloom/specular causal pair.
The user accepted old build brightness. These controls diagnose the complaint and do not imply visual acceptance or retail parity.
